classification.difficultyReason: Proves equal cross-sectional areas and uses Cavalieri’s principle to derive the sphere-volume formula.

inlines.text: Cavalieri’s principle states that if we have two solids of the same height and the cross-sections of each solid taken at the same distance from the base have the same area, then the solids have the same volume. Take a hemisphere of radius
and look at the area of a typical cross-section at height
Also, consider a cylinder of height
, with a cone cut out of it, also of height
. We also take a cross-section at height

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the radius of the circular cross-section of the sphere at height $h$ is $\sqrt{r^2-h^2}$.

answer.worked:
Let the cross-section radius be $x$. The diagram gives a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $r$ and legs $h$ and $x$:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+h^2&=r^2\\x^2&=r^2-h^2\\x&=\sqrt{r^2-h^2}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Deduce that the area of the cross-section is $\pi(r^2-h^2)$.

answer.worked:
Using the radius from part a,
$$\begin{align*}A&=\pi x^2\\A&=\pi\left(\sqrt{r^2-h^2}\right)^2\\A&=\pi(r^2-h^2).\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Draw a diagram of the cross-section of the cylinder with the cone removed, and show that the area of the cross-section at height $h$ is also $\pi(r^2-h^2)$.

answer.short: An annulus with outer radius $r$ and inner radius $h$; its area is $\pi r^2-\pi h^2=\pi(r^2-h^2)$.
answer.worked:
The cylinder’s section is a circle of radius $r$. The removed cone’s section has radius $h$, as shown in the supplied diagram. The remaining section is an annulus:
$$\begin{align*}A&=A_{\text{outer circle}}-A_{\text{inner circle}}\\A&=\pi r^2-\pi h^2\\A&=\pi(r^2-h^2).\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete solution plan view: concentric circles with outer radius r and removed inner radius h. Light blue identifies only the remaining annular section.

children.label: d
children.prompt: We now conclude that the two solids have the same volume, by Cavalieri’s principle. Find the volume of the cylinder minus the cone.

answer.worked:
Both the cylinder and the removed cone have base radius $r$ and height $r$:
$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{remaining}}&=\pi r^2\times r-\frac13\pi r^2\times r\\V_{\text{remaining}}&=\pi r^3-\frac13\pi r^3\\V_{\text{remaining}}&=\frac23\pi r^3.\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: Deduce the formula for the volume of the sphere.

answer.short:
$V=\dfrac43\pi r^3$.

A sphere has twice the volume of the hemisphere.
answer.worked:
By Cavalieri’s principle, the hemisphere has volume $\frac23\pi r^3$. A sphere consists of two such hemispheres:
$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{sphere}}&=2\times\frac23\pi r^3\\V_{\text{sphere}}&=\frac43\pi r^3.\end{align*}$$
